archetype_line: Fair point, delivered like a parking ticket appeal.

strengths.text: You put a real give before the ask: 'I'll throw in for tip and tax.' That is what keeps a boundary from sounding stingy. Dev's trust moved from 44 to 60 right after it, which suggests it landed.

You answered Dev's actual question. He said 'I'm curious what you've got in mind' and you came back with a specific figure ('I'll Venmo you twenty eight') instead of circling. Turn 2 had zero fillers, zero hedges and zero apologies.

change.text: Turn 1 had the right idea buried under three fillers, a hedge and a closing 'Sorry'. The apology is what cost you. Dev's likely read was 'He folded fast', which is why he pushed back with 'bailing'. Open with the turn 2 version: reason, number, done.
change.quote: Uh, I mean, I only had a salad, so, like, maybe we could do it by what we ordered? Sorry.

hint: Say the reason and the number in one sentence, and end on the number instead of on 'Sorry'. Cut 'uh, I mean, like, maybe'. Being friendly is fine, but you don't owe anyone an apology for ordering a salad.
example: I had a salad and water, so I'll put in twenty-eight plus my share of tip.

alternatives.line: Happy to cover tip and tax, but I only had a salad, so twenty-eight is my number. Steaks can split the rest.
I'll pay for what I ate, plus tip. Twenty-eight.

turning_point.quote: Look, I'll throw in for tip and tax, but ninety for a salad is wild. I'll Venmo you twenty eight.
turning_point.what_changed: Dev went into this turn doubting you ('Less convinced now', trust 44). Your concession plus a specific number gave him something to accept instead of argue with. His private thought became 'Clean ask, clear number', and trust rose to 60.

awareness.evidence: You answered the actual question (the split) and gave the reason in turn 1. In turn 2 you used Dev's own opening ('what you've got in mind') and came back with a concrete figure and a concession on tip and tax. You asked nothing back, and there was little need to. You lose points because turn 1 read the moment as 'smooth this over' instead of 'state the fact', and Dev picked up on it.

script: Turn one was three fillers, a hedge and a Sorry stapled to a perfectly fair point. Dev's likely read: you folded fast. Turn two fixed it: no padding, a number, a concession on tip and tax, and trust went from 44 to 60. You had the good version in you the whole time. Open with it: number first, no sorry.

turns.text: Easiest thing is we just split it six ways, right? Like ninety each.
Uh, I mean, I only had a salad, so, like, maybe we could do it by what we ordered? Sorry.
Oh, come on, that's the fair call, nobody's making you apologize for a salad. Honestly though, sounds like you're bailing on the whole even-split thing, so I'm curious what you've got in mind.
Look, I'll throw in for tip and tax, but ninety for a salad is wild. I'll Venmo you twenty eight.
Twenty-eight works, and I'll take the Venmo, but you're buying the next round of waters.

trace.thought: Apologizing for a salad? He folded fast. Less convinced now.
Clean ask, clear number. That's how it should've gone from the start.
